patient.name: Daniel Ortiz
patient.chiefComplaint: Cardiac arrest following high-voltage electrical contact

history.hpi: Maintenance electrician contacted an overhead high-voltage line while working on a catwalk, was thrown approximately 8 feet by the resulting muscle contraction, and found down by coworkers. Power was confirmed shut off at the breaker before bystanders began CPR.
history.lastOralIntake: Lunch approximately 2 hours prior to the incident
history.events: Coworkers heard a loud snap and saw the patient thrown from an overhead high-voltage line; they shut off power at the breaker panel before starting bystander CPR and calling 911

scene.dispatch: 37-year-old male, electrical injury, unresponsive, industrial site
scene.location: Warehouse maintenance catwalk near an overhead high-voltage electrical panel
scene.safety: Power confirmed off at the breaker by the facility electrician prior to EMS approach; scene otherwise secure
scene.bystanders: Two coworkers present; one performed bystander CPR after cutting power, reports sudden muscle contraction and fall from the contact point
visualCues: Entry wound with charred tissue at the right palm
Exit wound at the left heel with a soot/burn pattern
Coworkers standing by the breaker panel
Bystander CPR in progress on arrival

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew arrives to find a 37-year-old male in cardiac arrest following high-voltage electrical contact. Bystander CPR is in progress; coworkers confirm the power source has been shut off and the scene is safe to approach.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: No palpable pulse on primary survey
otherFindings: Entry wound with charring at right palm
Exit wound with burn pattern at left heel

expectedActions.shortAction: Identify and treat dysrhythmia/arrest from electrical contact per Cardiac Arrest protocol
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Identify dysrhythmias or cardiac arrest — even patients who appear dead (particularly dilated pupils) may have good outcomes with prompt intervention
expectedActions.rationale: Electrical arrest patients can have good outcomes with prompt, standard ACLS care.

expectedActions.shortAction: Resume high-quality chest compressions immediately, minimize interruptions
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Initiate chest compressions in cases with no bystander chest compressions or take over compressions from bystanders while a second rescuer is setting up the AED or defibrillator
expectedActions.rationale: Effective, minimally interrupted compressions are the foundation of resuscitation from VF.

expectedActions.shortAction: Defibrillate coarse VF at maximum biphasic setting per manufacturer (e.g., 200 J)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Defibrillation dosing should follow manufacturer's recommendation in the case of biphasic defibrillators. If the manufacturer's recommendation is unknown, use highest setting possible.
expectedActions.rationale: Prompt defibrillation is the single most important therapy for a shockable rhythm.

expectedActions.shortAction: Apply continuous cardiac monitor and obtain 12-lead EKG as soon as feasible
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Perform primary survey with specific focus on dysrhythmias or cardiac arrest — apply a continuous cardiac monitor and obtain 12-lead EKG as soon as feasible
expectedActions.rationale: Electrical injury carries high risk of ongoing dysrhythmia even after the initial rhythm is addressed.

expectedActions.shortAction: Epinephrine 1 mg IV/IO during the first or second compression cycle
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: If feasible, IV or IO access should be obtained. Administer Epinephrine 1mg during the first or second round of compressions.
expectedActions.rationale: Early epinephrine supports coronary perfusion pressure during ongoing CPR.

transitions.condition: Crew confirms pulselessness, takes over compressions, and delivers the first defibrillation for coarse VF while establishing IV/IO access.
Crew pauses compressions and defibrillation to examine and dress the entry/exit burn wounds before addressing the shockable rhythm, delaying definitive treatment.

phases.name: CPR and defibrillation initiated
phases.description: Crew confirms pulseless VF, resumes high-quality chest compressions, and delivers manufacturer-recommended defibrillation while establishing IV/IO access for epinephrine.
phases.triggerCondition: After confirming pulselessness and coarse VF on the monitor, the crew immediately resumes chest compressions, applies pads, and delivers the first defibrillation without interrupting compressions for burn assessment.

clinicalPresentation.airway: OPA in place, passive ventilation via NRB
otherFindings: Defibrillation pads placed avoiding burn sites

expectedActions.shortAction: Treat per Post-ROSC Care Guideline: titrate oxygen to SpO2 94-98%, avoid hyperventilation
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: If at any time during this period of resuscitation the patient regains return of spontaneous circulation, treat per Adult Post-ROSC Care Guideline
expectedActions.rationale: Hyperoxia and hyperventilation after ROSC worsen neurologic outcome.

expectedActions.shortAction: Identify and dress entry (right palm) and exit (left heel) burn wounds with dry dressings
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Apply dry dressing to any wounds
expectedActions.rationale: Entry/exit sites mark the current path and often underrepresent deep tissue damage.

expectedActions.shortAction: Assess for compartment syndrome from extremity tissue damage
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Assess for potential compartment syndrome from significant extremity tissue damage
expectedActions.rationale: Deep tissue injury from electrical current can far exceed external appearance.

expectedActions.shortAction: Apply spinal motion restriction given the fall from the contact point
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Apply spinal motion restriction if associated trauma suspected
expectedActions.rationale: The muscle-contraction fall mechanism carries real risk of spinal injury.

expectedActions.shortAction: Transport to a burn center capable of managing electrical injury; report voltage/AC-DC characteristics to receiving facility
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Electrical injury patients should be taken to a burn center whenever possible since these injuries can involve considerable tissue damage
expectedActions.rationale: Electrical burns are often full-thickness with damage that isn't apparent externally.

transitions.condition: After the second defibrillation and continued high-quality CPR with epinephrine on board, the patient regains a palpable pulse and organized rhythm.

phases.name: ROSC achieved, burns addressed
phases.description: The patient regains return of spontaneous circulation with an organized sinus tachycardia. Crew now identifies and dresses the entry/exit burn wounds, assesses for associated trauma from the fall, and prepares for transport to a burn/trauma-capable center.
phases.triggerCondition: After ROSC, the crew shifts focus to the secondary survey, identifying the entry wound at the right palm and exit wound at the left heel, dressing both, assessing for compartment syndrome and fall-related trauma, and preparing for transport.

clinicalPresentation.breathing: Spontaneous but shallow, assisted with BVM
otherFindings: Entry wound at right palm dressed
Exit wound at left heel dressed
Distal pulses intact, assessed for compartment syndrome
Spinal motion restriction applied given fall from height

phases.name: Defibrillation delayed for burn assessment
phases.description: Crew becomes fixated on examining the dramatic entry/exit burn wounds and delays defibrillation, allowing VF to persist. Prolonged downtime without definitive rhythm treatment lowers the chance of a good outcome.
phases.triggerCondition: Compressions and pad placement are interrupted so the crew can inspect and photograph the burn wounds before delivering the indicated shock, delaying defibrillation by several minutes.

otherFindings: Burn wounds being examined instead of rhythm treated
CPR quality degraded during the interruption

expectedActions.shortAction: Recognize refractory VF from delayed defibrillation; resume compressions and shock immediately
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Successful resuscitation from cardiac arrest depends primarily on effective, minimally interrupted chest compressions and prompt defibrillation if the patient is in pulseless VT/VF.
expectedActions.rationale: Every minute of delayed defibrillation reduces the probability of successful resuscitation.

expectedActions.shortAction: Amiodarone 300 mg IV/IO for refractory VF after continued shocks
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Amiodarone 300mg, followed by 150mg 4-6 min later if still in refractory VF and pulseless VT
expectedActions.rationale: Antiarrhythmic therapy is indicated once VF persists despite CPR and defibrillation.
